ABI text = string (UTF-16 code units). Every character of CODE is a single ASCII code unit, so scanning code units is
  identical to scanning code points; a surrogate pair is never split or touched. Result: a string. The artifact is an ES

  ('' + str, ToPrimitive with the default hint), then R1-R4 apply. Hence 42 -> "42", null -> "null", true -> "true",
  undefined -> "undefined", -0 -> "0", an array -> its elements joined by "," (codes inside them then stripped), a

  wins over toString), a bigint -> its digits; a symbol THROWS a TypeError. A lone surrogate is kept like any other
  character.

  non-overlapping, resume-after-match scan and replace's single pass gives R4. \d in a regex without the u flag (and
  with it) is ASCII-only, matching DIGIT.

  over valueOf) and String(symbol) does not throw.

DESCRIPTION Remove the single-parameter SGR color codes (ESC "[" decimal digits "m") that colors.js itself emits, leaving
  every other character of the text untouched. It is NOT a general ANSI stripper: combined SGR ("ESC[1;31m"), other CSI
  sequences ("ESC[2J") and OSC sequences ("ESC]0;title BEL") pass through unchanged.
BEHAVIOR
R1 The result is the input text with every CODE occurrence (R2, R3) removed; every other character is kept, in order,
  unchanged. A text containing no CODE is returned as is; the empty text yields the empty text.
R2 A CODE is a contiguous span matching the grammar CODE (PINNED below): the ESCAPE character U+001B, then "[" (U+005B),
  then one or more ASCII decimal digits, then a lowercase "m" (U+006D). The digit run has no length limit and leading
  zeros are allowed ("ESC[0000m" is a CODE). No parameter separator, no other final letter, no uppercase "M", no
  non-ASCII digit, and no empty digit run.
  CITED FIDELITY package — the package removes only this single-parameter SGR form; combined SGR, other CSI and OSC survive
R3 Occurrences are found leftmost-first and do not overlap: scanning from the start, at each position where a CODE
  begins, the whole CODE (the digit run taken in full) is removed and scanning resumes immediately after its "m".
  Where no CODE begins, the character is kept and scanning moves on by one character.
R4 The removal is ONE pass and is never repeated: a CODE that only comes into existence because a removal joined the
  text around it is kept ("ESC[" + "ESC[1m" + "31m" yields "ESC[31m").
  CITED FIDELITY package — a single global replacement, not a fixed-point loop
PINNED grammar CODE = ESC "[" DIGIT+ "m" CITED R2 — colors@1.4.0 strip; ESC = U+001B, "[" = U+005B, DIGIT = one of U+0030..U+0039 (the ten ASCII digits only), "m" = U+006D only; a C1 CSI U+009B does not begin a CODE
INVARIANT the result never contains a CODE that was present in the input; its length is the input's length minus the
  total length of the removed CODE spans; text with no U+001B is returned unchanged.

DEPENDS-ON none
DESCRIPTION Decide whether a value is a finite number, or text that parses as one.
BEHAVIOR
R1 a primitive number that is finite -> true; NaN and ±Infinity -> false. (-0 is finite -> true.)
R2 primitive text that is non-empty after trimming whitespace and parses as a finite number -> true.
R3 everything else -> false (booleans, none, non-numeric or empty text).
R4 a boxed wrapper (a Number object, a String object) is not a primitive -> R3 -> false. CITED FIDELITY package — the primitive/boxed accident of is-number@7.0.0 (js-only; outside other languages' envelope)
INVARIANT the result is a boolean for every input in the envelope.
